v.why: A strong direct conv path to the output saturates accuracy, so extra convs on internal edges add little.
Parallel convs into the output node are redundant, so the second one gains less.
Edges 0 and 1 both feed early features, so a conv on one makes a conv on the other partly redundant.
A strong conv path into the output already exists, so the added skip helps less.
A conv on edge 4 already supplies a strong route to the output, so the skip's marginal benefit is smaller.
A conv on edge 0 already provides strong early features, so another conv from the input adds less.
Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already absent leaves fewer routes to the output, so the loss is larger.
Without the direct edge, output quality depends on the node-2 path, so improving edge 5 matters more.
With no direct input-to-output edge, an extra skip into node 3 gives a shortcut that is otherwise missing.
Adding the direct input-to-output skip where none existed greatly improves gradient flow compared with replacing another op.
